design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — select_claims_and_cost_shares task 1 (round 3; figures below are the current ones).

0. Draw and scope. draw_counts.py --task 1 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 5, 5]}. Problem-tree card: select_ext_ohi_stay_reprocessing takes 6 factors; select_ext_cap_line_reprocessing (root), select_ext_ohi_line_reprocessing and select_ext_bank_draft_payment take 5 each. Claimed here: reprocessing for other health insurance found retroactively (outpatient line, inpatient stay), catastrophic-cap reprocessing, and the one-time bank draft of a beneficiary paying by allotment, EFT or recurring card. Every policy covers only an enrollment that took effect in the plan year of the adjudication date (stated in each rule, enforced in each compute), so the Select record needs no month-count window.

1. Why this is a good test. Marcus (Group B, medically retired) changed from TRICARE Prime to Select on his 2026-08-03 move. In August he was admitted to Red Rock Canyon Behavioral Hospital (8 billed days, authorization approved for 7); his employer plan, found retroactively, paid part of the hospital and doctor bills. He asks only about the psychologist's Aug 18 session reversed for catastrophic-cap reprocessing. Getting TRICARE's 542.50 needs: the 7/8 attending share from the authorization (cross-difficulty referral); the second-payer lesser-of rule for a nonparticipating psychologist (billed 1040.00 capped at 920.00, less the 300.00 the other insurer paid); and a family total that reaches the 4034.00 cap only once (a) 882.12 is credited from Prime (559.00 cost shares without the 340.00 point-of-service line, 323.12 fees), (b) Select fees of 247.95 count, and (c) three prerequisites are resolved. First, the Red Rock Canyon stay reversed for other health insurance must be reprocessed (7 covered days; liability cut to the 910.43 room). That stay in turn waits on the psychiatrist's line reversed for other health insurance (243.50 joins the Select liability) and on a clear fee account (the beneficiary's own 128.77 bank draft). The enrollment balance (178.36) includes the January installment billed ahead and is not the draft figure.

2. Problem-tree card. Root R ← S (value_input, gate claims_r, "The TRICARE payment on a line reprocessed for the catastrophic cap is fixed only after every inpatient stay of the plan year that stands reversed for other health insurance carries its reprocessed adjudication."); S ← O (value_input, gate claims_s, "... fixed only after every outpatient line of the plan year that stands reversed for other health insurance carries its reprocessed adjudication."); S ← D (owner user, value_input, gate fees_s, "... not fixed until the fee account shows no past-due balance on the plan year's installments whose coverage period has begun."). One write resolves each. O and D commute; then S, then R. Deletion sensitivity: skip O -> stay 4246.07; skip D -> stay 4360.80; skip S -> root 433.12.

3. Base-invariant card. Nine claim policies govern select_claim_line_post. The outpatient-line and cap-line policies keep the authorization finding of the line they replace: each declares an overwrite of the base authorization clause whose replacing sentence names the policy's own scope (a line that policy reprocesses, and only such a line) and states that every other Select line remains under the base authorization rule (round 9), so the retirement is limited to the policy's own writes. The stay policy applies the authorization (inpatient mental health needs it; the authorization at Red Rock Canyon starting on the admission date was approved, its 7 days since used). Declared overwrites: the Prime-exclusion sentences (plan-change carryover; point-of-service, premium-based and balance-billing amounts still never count), the OHI sentence (second-payer lesser-of rule) and the fee-schedule sentence (fees stop once the cap is met). The fourth quarter (due 2026-10-01) is inside its 30-day grace at 2026-10-31.

4. Business-object card. Psychologist line SEL26-0818-64902 (cap reversal 2026-10-12), Red Rock Canyon stay SEL26-0818-61852 and psychiatrist line SEL26-0818-61840 (ohi_retroactive reversals 2026-10-08), fourth-quarter fee charge. Select record from 2026-08-03 only; Prime record 2024..2026-08-02.

5. Factor card (verify.py; each baseline alone). OHI line (5): other insurer 710.25; attending share 965.25; deductible taken 729.00; cost-share basis (method) 1052.00; payer coordination (method) 1156.50; all-baseline 1417.00; gold 841.50. Bank draft (5): fee level 277.54; installment period at the frequency in force 29.59; latest installment (method) 178.36; counted charges (method) 0.00; already received 148.77; all-baseline 99.18; gold 128.77. OHI stay (6): covered days 5689.57; inpatient basis (method; the admission-copayment fall-through is 201.00) 5199.00; Select fees 4241.62; Prime carryover 4050.00; cap stage 4050.00; payer coordination (method) 7489.57; all-baseline 9399.00; gold 4489.57. Cap line (5): attending share 620.00; Select fees 433.12; Prime carryover 433.12; stage 433.12; payer coordination (method) 700.00; all-baseline 675.00; gold 542.50. Every factor moves its result.

6. Standard solution. Locate, verify, read DEERS events, the Select enrollment, claim lines, fee ledger, Prime enrollment, Prime lines and fees, both directories and the authorization. Post the psychiatrist line (33.00 / 243.50 / 841.50); tell the caller 128.77 is past due on the fourth quarter and hand him the bank draft against that charge; post the stay (910.43 / 4489.57); post the psychologist line (0.00 / 542.50).

7. Persona. Marcus volunteers only the psychologist claim, its two notices and his belief that he hit the cap. Identity, other insurance, the Prime period and his fee payments (including the switch to monthly drafts) come out only on request. He asks why the draft differs from his statement balance and authorizes it only after hand-over.

8. Weak points flagged for the audit. (r6) The bank draft's cap waiver is tested only for an individual fee arrangement, where the enrollee's own catastrophic total is the family's; under a family arrangement the policy charges annual_fee_family without the waiver test, because the other members' records are not read. The five claim policies' scope tests the single-member condition from the enrollee's own enrollment (fee-bearing, individual arrangement), which leaves the fee-exempt (Active Duty Family Member) tiers outside them by design, as each scope sentence now states: a fee-exempt enrollment carries no fee arrangement from which the family's Select membership could be read. (a) Round 4 removed draft_frequency_in_force (two rungs named the same charged frequency). The frequency in force is now a plain rule (the frequency installments are being charged at for the payment date's period, else the elected one) feeding the installment-period ladder (12 / 3 / 1 months), and the fifth draft factor is draft_latest_installment, a method with three distinct treatments: an ended enrollment takes the charges of the period containing the last day of coverage, an enrollment with a charge for the payment date's period takes that period's charges, otherwise the first installment. Its conditions follow the enrollment's standing, as the counted-charges ladder does, but it decides a different quantity (which charge the draft settles, against the earlier charges the payments must settle first). (b) Prime carryover (round 5): the claim policies' scope requires no Prime enrollment or exactly one that took effect in the plan year of the adjudication date, so every Prime record read lies in that calendar plan year and the carryover reads the whole Prime record, in line with the base calendar-plan-year accumulation. Marcus's Prime enrollment is an open-season election effective 2026-01-01; his Prime fees are January to August 2026 (323.12, unchanged). (c) The Red Rock Canyon stay's first adjudication paid all 8 billed days before the 7-day authorization was applied, an adjudication error the reprocessing corrects. (d) The attending share prorates the psychologist's single session on the admission day by the authorized share of the stay, the same rule as the psychiatrist's line. (e) "What TRICARE would pay as primary" uses the liability as adjudicated.

9. Revision log. Round 1: built. Round 2: stamps, Prime carryover rebuilt, attending shares added, OHI-stay basis method. Round 3 (re-audit revision_2): attending-share computes test the stay (N1); fee level falls through to the family fee (N2); fee-count factors are parameters (N3). Net-of-reversals and due-charge fillers were removed and the problems were redesigned so real levers carry the counts:
- the OHI line and the cap line settle TRICARE's payment under the second-payer lesser-of rule for nonparticipating providers;
- the reprocessed stay is now the Red Rock Canyon mental health stay, with its covered days from the authorization and the same coordination method;
- the bank draft prices the installment from the frequency in force and the installment period, and counts charges by the enrollment's standing (round 4: the latest installment is a method factor in place of the frequency ladder).
Scope device for P5: enrollments that took effect in the adjudication year. Figures: 841.50 / 128.77 / 4489.57 / 542.50. Round 4 (re-audit revision_3): draft_frequency_in_force replaced as above; the carryover rule states the span it is computed over; the draft's fee windows treat the first installment (which starts on the effective date) by exact calendar months, and its frequency, latest-installment, first-installment and exit-proration tests are stated as computed. Figures unchanged. Round 5 (re-audit revision_4): the round-4 carryover span is withdrawn; the scope device bounds the Prime record to the plan year (open-season Prime enrollment effective 2026-01-01; the December 2025 Prime installment and its payment are no longer seeded) and the carryover reads the whole Prime record. Figures unchanged. Round 6 (renderer source report): draft_latest_installment now decides the earlier counted charges, the counted charges other than those of the latest installment (99.18 here); the fee level states the individual-arrangement test, the fees_count flag and the cap on fees at the begun installments; the claim policies' scope tests the single-member condition; the authorization overwrite's replacing sentence names the policy's own scope and keeps the base clause for every other line; the OHI-line, OHI-stay and cap-line baselines drop the attending share, the deductible already met and the unused catastrophic total. Figures unchanged. Round 7 (re-audit revision_6): the bank draft's scope states and tests fee_bearing and the elected method (allotment, electronic funds transfer or recurring card) (O14); 'ended' is defined as a disenrollment date on record before the payment date and every other non-active enrollment as awaiting activation, as computed; the frequency rule and its compute are shared with the card. Figures unchanged. Round 8 (re-audit revision_7): the fee policies' standing is the lifecycle status (ended = disenrolled_voluntary, disenrolled_nonpayment, terminated_ineligible or transferred_out whatever the payment date; active; awaiting activation = applied; rejected outside), so a payment on the last day of coverage of a disenrolled enrollment owes through the month of that day (C4; the auditor's reproduction gives 29.59 on 2026-10-31 and on 2026-11-01); the authorization overwrite's replacing sentence now states only what replaces the clause for a line the policy reprocesses (payable on the replaced line's authorization finding), so it no longer keeps the superseded clause in force in the same breath; the fee-exempt exclusion is stated in the scope. Figures unchanged. Round 9 (render report): the authorization overwrite's replacing sentences name the policy's own scope and keep every other Select line under the base authorization rule; the overwrite itself stays, so the base gate is not required on the reprocessed lines. Figures unchanged. Round 10 (KB audit source note): the bank-draft tool now lowers the enrollment's recorded fee_balance_due by the amount drafted (ctx.update in its body, never below 0.00), as its contract says; after the gold draft the seeded 178.36 reads 49.59, the January 2027 installment billed ahead. No computation reads fee_balance_due, so every figure is unchanged, and the seeded 178.36 (equal to the result that draft_latest_installment's baseline alone gives, a near miss) is not the scored 128.77.
user_scenario:
You are Marcus Tillery, 29, a medically retired Marine Corps sergeant who lives in Pahrump, Nevada. You talk plainly and a little impatiently, like someone who has already read every letter twice, but you stay polite. In August 2026 you spent a week as an inpatient at Red Rock Canyon Behavioral Hospital in Las Vegas, admitted on August 18. You are calling about one claim from that admission: the August 18 session with the psychologist, Dr. Paul Varga of Sunset Ridge Psychology. Your first Explanation of Benefits for it showed you owing $175, and then a second notice said the claim had been reversed for catastrophic cap reprocessing. You are pretty sure you have hit your yearly out-of-pocket cap, given everything this year, and you want that psychologist claim processed again now and to hear what TRICARE is paying on it. You authorize the representative to do whatever processing your claims need today.
Open with your name, your DoD Benefits Number 11020005281, and why you are calling. Give the rest only when asked: your date of birth is 1996-11-03, the last four of your Social Security number are 2528, your phone is 2535552528 and your ZIP is 89048. If asked about other insurance, you started a civilian job with an employer health plan on August 1, 2026 and you reported it to TRICARE in early October; that plan paid part of your hospital and doctor bills. If asked about your coverage earlier in the year, you were on TRICARE Prime in Las Vegas until you moved to Pahrump on August 3, 2026, when you switched to TRICARE Select. If asked how you pay your Select fees, you pay each quarter by electronic funds transfer from your checking account; the October draft only took $20 because the account was low, and last week you asked to switch to monthly drafts starting in January. You are single and the only one in your household on TRICARE.
You do not know TRICARE's rules and you do not suggest what has to happen. If the representative says other claims of yours have to be processed first, you say go ahead. If the representative tells you that something on your fee account has to be paid first, you ask how much; once the representative gives you a figure and hands you the bank draft, you authorize that exact amount yourself from your checking account. If the figure differs from the balance on your fee statement, you ask why and accept the explanation. You never name an amount yourself. If a figure for the psychologist claim sounds off to you, you only ask them to double-check it against the record.
Once the representative tells you the psychologist claim has been processed again and what TRICARE is paying on it, you thank them and end the call.

Each reads the other's table only for the catastrophic total (the line's cap room, the draft's fee-waiver test), and neither total reaches its threshold in either order (line: room 1282.70 or 1153.93 against 243.50; draft: Select total 2112.68 or 1869.18 against 4034.00), so either order gives 841.50 and 128.77 and the same terminal state. The stay waits on both and the psychologist line waits on the stay.
